name: Taspoglutide

card.summary: An experimental once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist developed for type 2 diabetes that produced weight loss in trials but was discontinued, discussed in fat-loss circles as a precursor to semaglutide-type drugs.
card.note: Development was halted in 2010 over hypersensitivity and gastrointestinal side effects; not approved anywhere.

quick.overview:
Taspoglutide was a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist developed by Roche and Ipsen as a once-weekly injection for type 2 diabetes. GLP-1 drugs lower blood sugar and reduce body weight, which is why the class matters to people who want to lose fat and look leaner.

Trials showed improved glucose control and some weight loss, but the programme was stopped in 2010. It is now a historical step in the GLP-1 story rather than something available.
quick.how: It was developed as a subcutaneous injection given weekly in clinical trials. It was never approved, so it is not prescribed, and newer GLP-1 drugs have taken its place in the appearance-related conversation.
quick.risks: Roche halted phase III trials in September 2010 because of serious hypersensitivity reactions and gastrointestinal side effects. Pancreatitis cases during development were also discussed in reviews of the GLP-1 class.

lead: Taspoglutide (R1583/BIM51077) was an anti-diabetic drug from Hoffmann-La Roche, a long-acting analogue of human GLP-1 with 93% homology to the native peptide, meant to be given as a once-weekly subcutaneous injection [1].

It was relevant to looks because GLP-1 receptor agonists produce clinically meaningful weight loss alongside glucose control [2]. A model-based meta-analysis estimated placebo-adjusted weight loss from taspoglutide in diabetes trials [3].
Roche halted the phase III trials in September 2010 over serious hypersensitivity reactions and gastrointestinal side effects, and no new trials were registered after 2010 [4].

chain: Reduced appetite and improved glucose control
angle.text: Taspoglutide acted on the GLP-1 receptor, the same target as modern weight-loss drugs, and showed weight loss in diabetes trials, but it never reached the market.

paras: Taspoglutide is a modified GLP-1(7-36) amide that activates the GLP-1 receptor and was formulated for weekly or biweekly dosing [1].

Roche and Ipsen co-developed the drug, with eight phase III trials planned against exenatide, sitagliptin, insulin glargine and pioglitazone [4]. Roche stopped the trials in September 2010 over hypersensitivity and gastrointestinal events [4].
A review of GLP-1 agonists and pancreatitis covered clinical development data for taspoglutide among several agents [5]. The trial halt cited serious hypersensitivity and gastrointestinal events [4].

A 2009 review found six clinical studies, with significant improvements in glucose control and metabolic parameters [1]. A model-based meta-analysis estimated a maximal placebo-adjusted weight loss of about 1.85 kg versus 1.33 kg for placebo responses [3]. A 2012 review placed taspoglutide among five GLP-1 agonists in clinical development [2].

timeline.event: Review describes taspoglutide in phase III trials [1].
Roche halts phase III trials over hypersensitivity and gastrointestinal side effects [4].
